cold_open.title: TRANSFER ORDER
authoredText: The transport has no windows. Restraints hold your wrists to the bench; the guard across from you has stopped looking up.
A speaker reads the sentence aloud: the charge, the article, the reduction offered for every mission survived.
The door opens on the Correctional Command Program outpost. Someone is waiting with a clipboard.
headStartText: You sit down at the table and let the past come back: the charge, the article, the day the transport brought you here.
One night you lie awake and work out what your place is in this outpost: a convicted officer over soldiers who were built to be written off.
The weeks since have gone by with the squad. You put them in order, one by one, before the first operation begins.

lines.ask_crime: Article under which you were convicted?
lines.confirm_owner: Your sentence is held by {CORPORATION}. Confirm.

lines.intro: Stand on the mark. Arms out. This will take a minute.
lines.traits_note: Notes for the file. Two at most; the file keeps what it is given.

lines.sign_prompt: Review the file. Once it is signed, the file is filed and you deploy.

lineup.title: LINE-UP
lineup.directive: This is the first meeting between the commander and the squad, in the garage straight after arrival. Each soldier sizes up the commander in her own way and says so in character; none of them knows yet whether the commander is worth following. Keep it a first meeting: no mission talk, no promises.
lineup.objective: Stand before the squad at the line-up.

first_words.title: FIRST WORDS
first_words.directive: A short private exchange, the first time the commander and this soldier speak alone. She answers as herself and reveals one real thing about her attitude to the commander; keep it brief and leave the rest unsaid.
first_words.objective: Say a few words to each soldier.

tutorial.title: SHAKEDOWN PATROL
tutorial.objective: Take the shakedown patrol out and bring it back.

hints.text: Soldiers fight from the front or the back row. Melee reaches only the front while anyone stands there.
Command Points pay for your orders. You gain one each round; spend them when an order changes the fight.
Fights and danger raise stress. A strained soldier plays her defects harder, so watch the bars between nodes.

debrief.title: DEBRIEF
debrief.objective: File the after-action report for the patrol.

first_evening.title: FIRST EVENING
first_evening.objective: Spend the evening with whoever wants to talk.

nightKnock.framing: {name} is at the door, and it is not about duty.

authoredText: The transport smells of disinfectant and wet concrete. Restraints hold your wrists to the bench, and the guard across from you wears a Vesper Somatics sleeve patch.
A speaker reads the sentence aloud in a pleasant voice: the charge, the article, the reduction offered for every mission survived.
Through the slot of a window the District 7 quarantine wall goes by, green with growth. The Correctional Command Program outpost is the last clean building on the road.
A clerk waits at the gate with a clipboard and a sample case. The case, you are told, is not your concern yet.

lines.ask_crime: Article under which Vesper Somatics has convicted you?
lines.ask_name: Name for the record. The clean kind of record.
lines.confirm_owner: Your sentence is held by {CORPORATION}, and so is everything you are about to touch. Confirm.

lineup.directive: This is the first meeting between the commander and the squad, in the outpost garage, a few streets from the District 7 quarantine wall. Vesper Somatics assigned the unit to secure Bloom samples; the soldiers know they are off-spec assets under a convicted officer, and each says what she makes of that in character. Keep it a first meeting: no mission talk, no promises.
lineup.objective: Stand before the squad in the garage.

tutorial.objective: Walk the quarantine edge and bring the patrol back.

authoredText: The transport is a cargo carrier with benches welded to the floor. Restraints hold your wrists to a rail, and the guard across from you is mouthing numbers at the floor. Quotas, probably.
A speaker reads the sentence aloud, flat as a shift report: the charge, the article, the reduction offered for every mission survived.
Down the carrier ramp the Corridor K-12 mine mouth is a black seam in the hillside, with pylons and floodlights dragged up to it.
A foreman waits at the gate with a clipboard and a clock. The clock, you are told, is already running.

lines.ask_crime: Article under which Kestrel-Ward has convicted you?
lines.confirm_owner: Your sentence is held by {CORPORATION}. The quota is not negotiable. Confirm.

lineup.directive: This is the first meeting between the commander and the squad, in the outpost garage beside the Corridor K-12 mine road. Kestrel-Ward has set a quota deadline; the soldiers know they are expendable off-spec assets under a convicted officer, and each says what she makes of that in character. Keep it a first meeting: no mission talk, no promises.
lineup.objective: Stand before the squad in the garage.

tutorial.objective: Walk the corridor mouth and bring the patrol back.

warden_reveal.title: WARDEN BRIEFING
warden_reveal.objective: Meet the soldier who holds the controller.
warden_reveal.directive: AUTHOR TO WRITE: This is the first meeting between the commander and the warden. The corporation has put the controller of the commander's implant in her hands. She is a soldier of the squad, and she is neither cruel nor kind by default: she is under orders too. Show how she carries the controller and let the commander find out where they stand with each other.
authoredText: AUTHOR TO WRITE: By order of oversight, one soldier of the unit holds the controller of the commander's implant. Her orders are on file.
